messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I've uploaded the perf dump from last night's end-to-end run: block-bucket allocator + streaming-kernel fallback.
Alex: TL;DR: overall 6.4ms/token median for short sequences, but tail latency + OOMs show up on mixed workloads with long-context sessions.
Alex: baseline (old allocator): 7.8ms/token median, 48GB peak.
Alex: bucketized allocator v1: 6.4ms/token median, 52GB peak, but OOMs reduced from 4 -> 1 per hour on the testprofile.
Maya: Interesting. What changed exactly in the allocator? 
Alex: small-block pools for 8KB/32KB buckets, reusing 'evicted' blocks if age < 2s, and we avoid an immediate global compaction during concurrent KV writes.
Sam: Did you tune workspace sizing for the streaming kernels too?
Alex: Yes — streaming kernel uses dynamic workspace with 1.1x size for >512 tokens, falls back to compact kernels above 2048.
Ingrid: Any profiling traces for compaction cost? the compaction time is what's killing tails.
Alex: uploaded flamegraph and kvtrace snippets here: https://internal.redwood/p/perf/1823456789
Alex: snippet:
```
[compactor] compact_blocks()  92ms
copy_block_range()           48ms
allocate_workspace()         18ms
```
Maya: That 92ms is too high. Maybe compaction scanning is O(n) across blocks; can we limit scan window? 
Sam: Also the kernel selection path adds 2-3ms when switching kernels mid-request due to workspace reallocation.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: tail_p95 latency increased +18% when compaction runs > 50ms
Alex: Agree — plan A: lower compaction aggressiveness, increase reuse TTL to 4s, and move compaction work to async worker thread (non-blocking for request path).
Maya: Plan B: increase per-stream workspace by 1.2x and prefer streaming kernels (avoid mid-request kernel swap).
Ingrid: Quick A/B: I'll run 12hr mixed workload with bucket 64KB vs 128KB and workspace multipliers 1.1/1.2. Sam can enable kernel-selection logs (--kernel-debug=1) to capture swaps.
Sam: On it. command to reproduce:
```
./perf-run --profile=mixed_long_short --allocator=bucket_v1 --workspace-mult=1.2 --kernel-debug=1
```
Alex: If we still see OOMs, next step is to allow overflow to CPU pinned buffers as emergency fallback (very last resort).
Maya: ok filing a small RFC for async compaction + reuse_ttl bump. will link in this thread.
Sam: I'll drop kernel-selection traces into the perf bucket and annotate
Alex: thanks all. Will watch the 12hr run and post results.
